svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop — Interactive Botany Lesson
svg.desc: A static SVG learning interface that uses anchor-based navigation to simulate dropping word-tile labels onto a labeled diagram of a flower.

g.text: A simulated interactive botany lesson · Click a word-bank tile to place the label · Use Hint, Check or Reset below
↑ Figure 4.1 — Drag a word-bank tile onto any empty slot to label the part. Click a placed label again to clear it. ↑
Pick a label from the word bank below
Each tile shows a flower-part name. Click one to “drop”
it onto the matching empty slot in the diagram.
Each empty slot connects with an arrow to the part
of the flower it describes — drag in that direction.
Hint explains tricky parts · Check confirms your work
· Reset clears the board and starts over.
Pistil — the entire female reproductive structure (stigma + style + ovary).
Stamen — the entire male reproductive structure (anther + filament).
Stigma — sticky surface that catches pollen.
Style — connects the stigma to the ovary.
Ovary — contains ovules that become seeds after fertilization.
Anther — sac that produces and releases pollen grains.
Filament — slender stalk that holds the anther up.
Petal — colorful parts that attract pollinators.
Click any tile below to begin.
Static educational illustration · No JavaScript · All interactivity simulated with anchor / :target
Click tiles ↑ · Click HINT / CHECK / RESET on the right to reveal overlays
Look at the central column first
The pistil is the entire female reproductive structure — three parts make it up:
The male counterpart is a stamen
Tip: the highlighted rings on the diagram point at the pistil and stigma while this hint is open.
thin stalk holding up the anther
stigma + style + ovary — the female organ
All ten placements are correct · Great work! Try the Reset button to practice again.
Clear every placement on the diagram?
All ten labels will be removed from the slots.
Your progress will reset to 0 / 10 and the word bank will return to its initial state.
FULL ANSWER KEY · All 10 Parts Labeled
Match each word to its part:
→ Colorful outer leaf; attracts pollinators (bees, butterflies).
→ Green leaf-like structure that protected the flower as a bud.
→ The entire male reproductive organ = anther + filament.
→ The entire female reproductive organ = stigma + style + ovary.
→ The pollen-producing sac at the tip of the filament.
→ The thin stalk that lifts the anther into the wind / insect path.
→ Bulb at the base of the pistil; holds ovules that become seeds.
→ The slender tube connecting stigma to ovary (pollen tube grows through it).
→ Sticky top of the pistil that catches pollen grains for fertilization.
→ The thickened base where all flower parts (sepals, petals, stamens) attach.
